correct_completion: she went out to meet her friends.
full_sentence: Having finished her homework, she went out to meet her friends.
acceptable_variants: she then went out to meet her friends.
she went out to see her friends.

options.why_wrong: The participle clause 'Having finished' must refer to the subject of the main clause. Here the main clause is about the homework, so the clause dangles.

options.text: she is finishing her homework now.
options.why_wrong: 'Having finished' shows that the first action was completed before the main action. A present continuous main clause contradicts this sequence.

options.text: she went out to meet her friends.
she has went out to meet her friends.
options.why_wrong: The past participle of 'go' is 'gone', so the correct form is 'has gone'. 'Has went' is ungrammatical.

grammar_focus: Perfect participle clauses ('Having + past participle') and subject agreement
explanation: A perfect participle clause describes an action completed before the action in the main clause, and its implied subject must be the same as the subject of the main clause. Ukrainian speakers should check this subject match carefully, because the sentence structure does not always map directly onto their first language.
translation: Закінчивши домашнє завдання, вона вийшла зустрітися з подругами.
